root_cause.text: In the SCTP_SENDALL path of sctp_sendmsg(), list_for_each_entry_safe() caches the next association (@tmp) before calling sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc(), which may drop the socket lock; the cached @tmp is not revalidated after re-acquiring the lock, so a concurrent peel-off or free of that association can lead to use-after-free or list type confusion.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and patch description state that "sctp_wait_for_sndbuf() revalidates @asoc ... but nothing revalidates @tmp. After a successful return, the iterator advances to the stale @tmp, yielding either a use-after-free ... or a list-walk onto the new endpoint's list head (type confusion)." The fix adds a re-derivation of @tmp from @asoc after sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc() returns.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix stale pointer issue by re-deriving the association list cursor after a potential socket lock release in sctp_sendmsg error handling.
intent_record.what: Added a comment and assignment `tmp = list_next_entry(asoc, asocs);` after `iov_iter_revert` in the error handling path of sctp_sendmsg.
intent_record.how: This re-derives the cached list cursor `tmp` from the validated `asoc` pointer, ensuring that subsequent list iteration continues correctly after the socket lock was potentially released and other associations may have been removed.
